lines.text: The summons comes from Halsey, which is normal, about a contract from the executive floor, which is not. He tells you this in his office with the door shut, in a voice that is trying to be neutral and failing.

Katherine Keller’s office has assigned you a contract. Personally. Executive Vice President. I have never met her, Abbott, and I have been here sixteen years; her office sends instructions, and the instructions arrive signed. This one came with a note. Four years with us, tier 3 in under four, zero losses, a handful of deviations the note says she ‘finds she doesn’t mind’. Do you know why that frightens me?

choices.text: “Because I don’t lose cargo, and people who don’t lose cargo get noticed.”

lines.text: Partly. Lots of people don’t lose cargo. Fewer people don’t lose cargo and don’t ask what it is. You asked, early on. The note says you’ve stopped. Her office finds that more interesting than if you’d never asked at all. I find it more worrying.
Someone up there has read every line in your file and understood every one. You keep your face where it is.

I will. It frightens me because her office has noticed exactly when you stopped asking questions, Abbott. The file shows the date. People who learn are more use to that floor than people who never needed to.
Someone up there has read every line in your file and understood every one. You keep your face where it is.
The silence that follows is not long. It is simply total.

Site 19 was a consolidation. You flew it well. If there was anything else about site 19 you wished to mention, courier, this would be the moment to decide not to, and I would be grateful if you decided not to in my office.
You decide not to. You feel the decision go into your file like a stamp.

The contract is an escort run. Sovereign key material, Rigel to the Secure Backbone node at Thule, with a NovaFoundry escort that has authority over the route. The note says, and I am reading it, ‘consider it a conversation we are having without either of us needing to speak.’ I don’t know what that means. I suspect you will.

I’ve watched three couriers get noticed by that floor in nine years as director. Two of them fly for her now and I don’t know what they fly. The third one I don’t know anything about at all. I can’t protect you from the executive floor. I want you to hear me say that, so you don’t ever think I’m trying.

choices.text: “You’ve protected me more than you know, Director.”

lines.text: Aboard ALC-7293, the escort contract is already on your private board. No client. A code. A route to a Secure Consortium Backbone node you have never heard of, and a signature block with a name on it you have only ever seen typed: Katherine Keller.
Aggie. Did you hear all that?

That is the whole of her reply. Four years ago she would have had a page of it. You are beginning to understand that the page is still there. She is simply waiting to be asked for it, and you have got out of the habit of asking.
